Below is a consolidated, practical 12‑week postpartum return-to-exercise program for your 33‑year‑old client who is 4 weeks post uncomplicated C‑section. It combines progressive strength, core rehabilitation, cardio (including a conservative introduction to HIIT), and a breastfeeding-friendly nutrition framework. It assumes: OB clearance for light activity now (walking), formal recheck at ~6 weeks before advancing abdominal loading or heavier strength; always stop and regress for bulging at the midline, pelvic‑floor symptoms (leakage, heaviness, prolapse sensation), incision problems or pain. If any red‑flag symptoms appear at any time, pause progression and refer to a pelvic‑floor physiotherapist or her clinician.

Quick safety checklist (use every phase)
- Incision healed and pain manageable; no redness/drainage/fever.
- No new urinary/fecal leakage, pelvic heaviness or prolapse symptoms.
- No visible midline bulging/doming during low‑level head lifts or plank regressions.
- Breathe: inhalation to expand ribs, exhale during exertion while lightly engaging pelvic floor/TA. Never Valsalva.
- Nutrition/hydration: meet breastfeeding caloric needs (+~300–500 kcal/day), adequate protein (1.1–1.6 g/kg/day) and fluids.

Program overview (12 weeks)
- Weeks 1–2 (postpartum wk 4–5): Foundation — walking, breathing, pelvic floor reconnection, gentle activation. 3 short sessions/wk + daily walking.
- Weeks 3–4 (postpartum wk 6–7): Post‑6w OB check → start light strength (bodyweight), anti‑extension/anti‑rotation core. 3 sessions/wk; walking increased.
- Weeks 5–8 (postpartum wk 8–11): Progressive strength foundation: single‑leg work, more sets/volume, moderate conditioning. 3–4 sessions/wk.
- Weeks 9–12 (postpartum wk 12–15) — Phase 3 (intensity push): Higher intensity bodyweight strength, core progressions, conditioning including low‑impact HIIT introduction (conservative). 4 sessions/wk (3 strength + 1 conditioning/active recovery).

Detailed week‑by‑week summary

Weeks 1–2 (Weeks 4–5 postpartum) — Goals: healing, pelvic‑floor reconnection, walking base
Frequency: 3 short sessions/week + daily short walks (5–20 min)
Session length: 20–30 min

Session A — Mobility / Activation
- Diaphragmatic breathing + pelvic‑floor cueing 5 min (supine knees bent).
- Cat–cow 8–10 reps.
- Pelvic tilts 10–12 reps.
- Heel slides 8–10 each side.
- Glute bridge (small range) 2 × 8–10 (slow).
- Side‑lying hip abduction 2 × 10 each side.
- Seated tall marches 1–2 minutes.
Cooldown: pelvic floor relax breathing.

Session B — Walk + light mobility
- 10–20 minute easy walk.
- Calf raises 2 × 12; gentle thoracic/shoulder mobility 5–8 min.

Session C — Gentle core reconnection
- Diaphragmatic breathing + TA draw‑in 5 min.
- Dead bug (very small ROM)/heel taps 2 × 8–10 each side.
- Bird‑dog small range 2 × 6 each side.
- Clamshells 2 × 10–12 each side.
- Gentle hamstring/hip stretch.

Nutrition (start): Ensure ~+300 kcal/day over maintenance for breastfeeding; protein 1.1 g/kg/day minimum; hydrate and continue prenatal/postnatal vitamin as advised.

Weeks 3–4 (Weeks 6–7 postpartum) — Goals: begin safe strength, anti‑rotation work (after 6‑week OB clearance)
Frequency: 3 sessions/week; walking 20–30 min most days
Session length: 25–35 min

Session A — Lower emphasis
- Warmup breathing + hip mobility.
- Glute bridge (full ROM if no doming) 3 × 10–12.
- Supported Romanian hinge to chair 3 × 8–10.
- Reverse lunges (support if needed) 2–3 × 8 each side.
- Side‑lying clamshell 3 × 12.
- Standing calf raises 3 × 12–15.

Session B — Core & posterior chain
- Dead bug 3 × 8–10 each side (small → larger ROM).
- Bird‑dog 3 × 8 each side (3–5s holds).
- Wall Pallof press (towel/doorframe) 3 × 8–10s each side.
- Prone scapular retraction/mini supermans 3 × 10.
- Modified side plank (knee down) 2 × 15–20s each side if no doming.

Session C — Walk + mobility
- Brisk walk 20–30 min; mobility flow 8–10 min.

Nutrition: Continue breastfeeding caloric guideline (+300–500 kcal); include post‑workout snack (~20 g protein + carbs).

Weeks 5–8 (Weeks 8–11 postpartum) — Goals: develop strength foundations, unilateral stability, core progression
Frequency: 3–4 sessions/week (3 strength + optional conditioning)
Session length: 30–45 min

Typical split:
- Strength 1: Lower (glutes, single‑leg)
- Strength 2: Posterior chain + core
- Strength 3: Single‑leg & functional
- Optional: Conditioning/mobility short session

Exercises & progressions (examples)
- Single‑leg glute bridges 3 × 8–10 each.
- Step‑ups 3 × 10 each.
- Bulgarian split squats 3 × 8 each.

Why be cautious
- HIIT increases intra‑abdominal pressure and ground reaction forces (even with low‑impact variants), which can provoke pelvic‑floor dysfunction, urinary leakage, or diastasis‑related bulging if started too early.
- Breastfeeding mothers also have higher energy needs and may be at risk of fatigue; aggressive HIIT without adequate fueling/recovery may reduce milk supply or impair recovery.

Readiness checklist (use before first HIIT session)
- Cleared by OB for more intense exercise.
- No visible midline bulge with a gentle head‑lift test or during plank progression.
- Can hold a forearm plank on toes for 20–30s without doming.
- Can perform repeated single‑leg RDLs and split squats with control and minimal fatigue.
- Reports no urinary leakage, pelvic heaviness, or pain with higher‑effort walking or circuit work.
- Stable daily energy and adequate nutrition/hydration for breastfeeding.

How to start — conservative HIIT progression (example timeline)
- Week 10 (if all checks pass): Try 1 very low‑impact "HIIT‑style" session/week — 12–15 minutes total high‑effort time including warmup/cooldown. Use low‑impact moves (marching, fast stair/stroller pushes, step‑ups, bodyweight squats) and short intervals (20–30s work / 40–60s easy).
- Week 11: If symptom‑free, increase to 1 session with slightly longer work intervals (30–40s work / 30–60s rest) or increase total rounds.
- Week 12: Progress intensity by adding another short session (total 1–2/week) or by increasing work periods (40–60s) if pelvic floor remains symptom‑free.
- Beyond week 12–16: If all good and she desires, progress to higher intensity HIIT, include low‑impact plyometrics cautiously, or add more sessions — ideally after pelvic‑floor PT clearance if there were earlier issues.

Low‑impact HIIT sample session (safe starter)
- Warm‑up 5 min: easy walk, dynamic hip swings, arm circles, diaphragmatic breathing.
- Main: 12–15 min total (example 4 rounds)
  - Work 30s: fast high‑knee march or fast step‑ups to a moderate height (no jumping)
  - Rest 60s: easy walk or slow march
  - Repeat 4–6 rounds depending on fitness
- Cool‑down 5 min: easy walk, pelvic‑floor breathing, gentle stretches.
Notes: Maintain breathing (no Valsalva). If any leaking, heaviness or midline doming occur, stop and regress.

Progressions and examples (low → moderate impact)
- Level 1 (low impact): fast marching, brisk stroller pushes, step‑ups, alternating reverse lunges, fast bodyweight squats.
- Level 2 (reduced impact, higher intensity): mountain‑climber‑style slow variations, fast alternating step‑ups on higher step, quick lateral stepovers (no jumps), incline power walks.
- Level 3 (introduce plyometrics cautiously and only after pelvic‑floor clearance): small hops, jump squats, bounding — but only if pelvic floor/pelvic organ support is confirmed strong.

Monitoring during and after HIIT
- Track symptoms during session (urinary leakage, bulging at midline, pelvic heaviness, pain). If any appear, stop and regress.
- Check the next 24–48 hours for increased pelvic pressure, heavier bleeding, fatigue, or reduced milk supply. If any negative changes occur, reduce intensity/frequency and consult a pelvic‑floor PT or lactation expert if supply concerns persist.
- Use RPE rather than heart rate initially: aim for work intervals at RPE 7–8/10 and recoveries RPE 2–4/10.

Fueling/recovery considerations for HIIT while breastfeeding
- Ensure adequate calories: add ~200 extra kcal on HIIT days in addition to baseline breastfeeding requirement (+300–500 kcal/day).
- Pre‑workout snack: small carb + protein (e.g., banana + yogurt) 30–60 min before if possible.
- Post‑workout: protein + carbs within 60–90 min (Greek yogurt + fruit, smoothie with protein powder, sandwich).
- Hydrate before/during/after and have a water bottle while nursing.

Alternative conditioning if not ready for HIIT
- Longer brisk walks with intervals (low‑impact).
- Circuit conditioning with strength moves and short rest (moderate density).
- Pool workouts (if available and incision fully healed) — low impact, cardio benefit, pelvic‑floor friendly.

When to refer
- If any urinary/fecal leakage starts or worsens with HIIT.
- If there’s visible doming/abdominal bulge during or after high‑effort work.
- If pelvic pressure/heaviness develops or symptoms of prolapse occur.
- Refer to pelvic‑floor physical therapy for individualized rehabilitation and an advanced return‑to‑HIIT plan.

Practical next steps for you as trainer
- Run the readiness checklist at week 10–12 and perform simple tests (plank, gentle head lift, single‑leg control).
- If cleared and ready, program 1 low‑impact HIIT session/week in Phase 3 as outlined above and closely monitor symptoms for 2–4 weeks before increasing frequency/intensity.
- Keep the client’s nutrition on point (extra calories/protein on HIIT days) and encourage sleep/naps.

Below is a consolidated, practical 12‑week postpartum return-to-exercise program for your 33‑year‑old client who is 4 weeks post uncomplicated C‑section. It combines progressive strength, core rehabilitation, cardio (including a conservative introduction to HIIT), and a breastfeeding-friendly nutrition framework. If any red‑flag symptoms appear at any time, pause progression and refer to a pelvic‑floor physiotherapist or her clinician.

Quick safety checklist (use every phase)
- Incision healed and pain manageable; no redness/drainage/fever.
- No new urinary/fecal leakage, pelvic heaviness or prolapse symptoms.
- No visible midline bulging/doming during low‑level head lifts or plank regressions.
- Breathe: inhalation to expand ribs, exhale during exertion while lightly engaging pelvic floor/TA. Never Valsalva.
- Nutrition/hydration: meet breastfeeding caloric needs (+~300–500 kcal/day), adequate protein (1.1–1.6 g/kg/day) and fluids.

Program overview (12 weeks)
- Weeks 1–2 (postpartum wk 4–5): Foundation — walking, breathing, pelvic floor reconnection, gentle activation. 3 short sessions/wk + daily walking.
- Weeks 3–4 (postpartum wk 6–7): Post‑6w OB check → start light strength (bodyweight), anti‑extension/anti‑rotation core. 3 sessions/wk; walking increased.
- Weeks 5–8 (postpartum wk 8–11): Progressive strength foundation: single‑leg work, more sets/volume, moderate conditioning. 3–4 sessions/wk.
- Weeks 9–12 (postpartum wk 12–15) — Phase 3 (intensity push): Higher intensity bodyweight strength, core progressions, conditioning including low‑impact HIIT introduction (conservative). 4 sessions/wk (3 strength + 1 conditioning/active recovery).

Detailed week‑by‑week summary

Weeks 1–2 (Weeks 4–5 postpartum) — Goals: healing, pelvic‑floor reconnection, walking base
Frequency: 3 short sessions/week + daily short walks (5–20 min)
Session length: 20–30 min

Session A — Mobility / Activation
- Diaphragmatic breathing + pelvic‑floor cueing 5 min (supine knees bent).
- Cat–cow 8–10 reps.
- Pelvic tilts 10–12 reps.
- Heel slides 8–10 each side.
- Glute bridge (small range) 2 × 8–10 (slow).
- Side‑lying hip abduction 2 × 10 each side.
- Seated tall marches 1–2 minutes.
Cooldown: pelvic floor relax breathing.

Session B — Walk + light mobility
- 10–20 minute easy walk.
- Calf raises 2 × 12; gentle thoracic/shoulder mobility 5–8 min.

Session C — Gentle core reconnection
- Diaphragmatic breathing + TA draw‑in 5 min.
- Dead bug (very small ROM)/heel taps 2 × 8–10 each side.
- Bird‑dog small range 2 × 6 each side.
- Clamshells 2 × 10–12 each side.
- Gentle hamstring/hip stretch.

Nutrition (start): Ensure ~+300 kcal/day over maintenance for breastfeeding; protein 1.1 g/kg/day minimum; hydrate and continue prenatal/postnatal vitamin as advised.

Weeks 3–4 (Weeks 6–7 postpartum) — Goals: begin safe strength, anti‑rotation work (after 6‑week OB clearance)
Frequency: 3 sessions/week; walking 20–30 min most days
Session length: 25–35 min

Session A — Lower emphasis
- Warmup breathing + hip mobility.
- Glute bridge (full ROM if no doming) 3 × 10–12.
- Supported Romanian hinge to chair 3 × 8–10.
- Reverse lunges (support if needed) 2–3 × 8 each side.
- Side‑lying clamshell 3 × 12.
- Standing calf raises 3 × 12–15.

Session B — Core & posterior chain
- Dead bug 3 × 8–10 each side (small → larger ROM).
- Bird‑dog 3 × 8 each side (3–5s holds).
- Wall Pallof press (towel/doorframe) 3 × 8–10s each side.
- Prone scapular retraction/mini supermans 3 × 10.
- Modified side plank (knee down) 2 × 15–20s each side if no doming.

Session C — Walk + mobility
- Brisk walk 20–30 min; mobility flow 8–10 min.

Nutrition: Continue breastfeeding caloric guideline (+300–500 kcal); include post‑workout snack (~20 g protein + carbs).

Weeks 5–8 (Weeks 8–11 postpartum) — Goals: develop strength foundations, unilateral stability, core progression
Frequency: 3–4 sessions/week (3 strength + optional conditioning)
Session length: 30–45 min

Typical split:
- Strength 1: Lower (glutes, single‑leg)
- Strength 2: Posterior chain + core
- Strength 3: Single‑leg & functional
- Optional: Conditioning/mobility short session

Exercises & progressions (examples)
- Single‑leg glute bridges 3 × 8–10 each.
- Step‑ups 3 × 10 each.
- Bulgarian split squats 3 × 8 each.
- Supported single‑leg RDL 3 × 8 each.
- Bird‑dog with 5s holds 3 × 8 each.
- Dead bug progressed to larger ROM 3 × 8–10 each.
- Side plank knee → partial full 3 × 15–25s.
- Circuit day: 2–3 rounds of squat, reverse lunge, glute bridge, bird‑dog, short plank.

Cardio
- Two longer walks/week (30–45 min), one interval/hill session/week (low impact; 6–8 × 45–60s brisk walk efforts).

Nutrition: Protein 1.2–1.5 g/kg/day; carb around training; hydrate. Add ~100–200 kcal on higher volume days.

Weeks 9–12 (Phase 3 — Weeks 12–15 postpartum) — Goals: push intensity, feel strong by week 12
Frequency: 4 sessions/week (3 strength + 1 conditioning/active recovery); daily walking as practical
Session length: 40–55 min

Overall progression approach:
- Increase sets (3 → 4), reduce rests, add tempo/slow eccentrics (3–4s), increase unilateral volume and complexity, add longer core holds and higher density circuits. Introduce conservative low‑impact HIIT (see readiness checklist).

Weekly template (Day 1–4)
Day 1 — Lower strength (heavy-ish, unilateral emphasis)
- Single‑leg RDL 3–4 × 8–10 each (3–4s eccentric)
- Bulgarian split squat 3–4 × 8–12 each
- Single leg/elevated glute bridge 3–4 × 8–12
- Step‑ups with knee drive 3–4 × 8–12 each
- Calf complex 3 × 15–20

Day 2 — Upper/posterior chain + core
- Prone Y/T/I or posterior chain lifts 3 × 10–12
- Incline → full push‑up progression 3–4 × 6–10
- Towel/door rows 3–4 × 8–12
- Dead bug advanced 3 × 10 each side
- Forearm plank progression 3 × 30–45s
- Pallof presses 3 × 10–12s each side

Day 3 — Conditioning / Active recovery
- Option A: Low‑impact HIIT starter (see readiness) 12–15 min main (30s work / 60s rest) OR
- Option B: Brisk steady walk 35–45 min with pickups
- Mobility 8–10 min

Day 4 — Full‑body strength circuit + core finisher
- Circuit 3–5 rounds (squats, single‑leg bridges, Bulgarian split, rows/push, plank) rest 60–90s between rounds.
- Core finisher: dead bug, side plank holds, Pallof holds.

Phase 3 weekly progression specifics
- Week 9: baseline — 3 sets mostly, 60–90s rest, moderate intensity.
- Week10: 4 sets on main lifts or reduced rest (45–60s), increased unilateral work.
- Week11: increase time under tension (4s eccentrics), add pauses/holds and higher circuit density.
- Week12: peak week — reduced rest, higher round counts, strength & conditioning benchmarks.

HIIT guidance (conservative)
- Readiness: OB clearance, no doming/bulging, good pelvic‑floor control, plank 20–30s on toes without doming, no leaking.
- Introduce 1 low‑impact HIIT session/week earliest around weeks 10–12 if cleared: 12–20 min total intervals (e.g., 6–8 × 30–45s work / 45–60s easy).
- Low‑impact work examples: fast marching, step‑ups, incline stroller pushes, controlled mountain climber regressions (no jumps).
- Monitor 24–48 hours for pelvic pressure, heavier bleeding or milk supply changes; regress if any issues.

Testing & benchmarks at end of Week 12
- Single‑leg RDL x10 controlled each leg.
- Bulgarian split squat 3 × 10 each leg with 2s pause bottom.
- Forearm plank 3 × 30–45s on toes without doming.
- Complete 3 rounds of full‑body circuit with 60–90s rest without symptoms.
- Improved subjective function: can lift/carry baby during daily tasks without pelvic heaviness or leakage.

Core reintegration timeline (summary)
- Weeks 1–6: breathing, pelvic floor, TA draw‑in, heel slides, very small dead bugs/bird‑dog — no direct anterior loading.
- Weeks 6–8: after clearance, add larger‑ROM dead bugs, gentle partial curl head lifts, Pallof anti‑rotation, knee planks.
- Weeks 8–12: increase plank duration/progression, longer partial curls, advanced dead bugs and standing chops; progress to full planks and dynamic core moves only if no bulge/leakage; after 12 weeks consider heavier anterior loading or weighted carries if pelvic floor/diastasis cleared.

Nutrition plan (breastfeeding-friendly)
Energy
- Add ~300–500 kcal/day to pre‑pregnancy maintenance while exclusively breastfeeding; adjust for activity and if weight‑loss desired do conservative deficit (≤0.5 kg/week) after supply stable.
- On high intensity days add extra 100–200 kcal.

Protein
- 1.1–1.6 g/kg/day (aim 1.2–1.6 g/kg while increasing strength). Spread across 3 meals + 1–2 snacks. Post‑workout snack: ~20–30 g protein + carbs.

Hydration & micronutrients

- Continue prenatal/postnatal vitamin unless advised otherwise.
- Ensure DHA (200–300 mg/day), vitamin D (per clinician), iodine (if not in prenatal), and iron if indicated.

Recovery & practical tips
- Prioritize sleep and naps; trade off overnight care when possible.
- Batch cook, keep easy high‑protein snacks accessible, bring water to feeds.
- Scar massage only after incision fully healed and clinician agrees.
- Encourage pelvic‑floor PT if any leakage or diastasis concerns.

Regressions (return to earlier phase if any symptom)
- Reduce ROM and intensity.
- Remove unilateral/loaded moves.
- Revert to supine TA activation and pelvic‑floor work until symptoms settle.
- Seek pelvic floor physiotherapy if persistent.
